requiredFacts.why: Verification decoders, evidence guards and protection broker checks must not be weakened by callers. Production isolation and draft dependency seams remain unproven.

part-nine FactEnvelope schema 1; owned-body schemas 1 and 2: createVerificationRuntime.record produces the exact v1 settlement body or v2 output-use body; decodeVerificationRecord, decodeVerificationRecordAtOrigin, and decodeHistoricalVerificationRecord preserve the signed version and refuse external migration wrappers. P9-NF-64, P9-NF-65, and P9-NF-66 are bounded build fixtures at tests/verification/provider-response-assessment.test.ts.

part-nine FactEnvelope schema 1; owned-body schemas 1 and 2: createProviderResponseAssessmentPort.assess produces the closed v2 output-use request through createVerificationRuntime.record while legacy producers retain v1; decodeVerificationRecord, decodeVerificationRecordAtOrigin, and decodeHistoricalVerificationRecord preserve exact identity and closure. P9-NF-64, P9-NF-65, and P9-NF-66 are bounded build fixtures at tests/verification/provider-response-assessment.test.ts.

part-nine FactEnvelope schema 1; owned-body schemas 1 and 2: createProviderResponseAssessmentPort.assess derives and records the exact six-row v2 output-use assessment while legacy settlement retains the four-row v1 body; decodeVerificationRecord, decodeVerificationRecordAtOrigin, and decodeHistoricalVerificationRecord validate the original owner basis. When that original verified register basis is unavailable, historical replay preserves the signed assessment only as evidence-unavailable under HOLD G6-NINE-HISTORICAL-REGISTER-BASIS and supplies no current authority. P9-NF-64, P9-NF-65, and P9-NF-66 are bounded build fixtures at tests/verification/provider-response-assessment.test.ts.
